podcast.title: CMA Song of the Year Winner (1976)
podcast.body: Larry Weiss won the CMA Song of the Year award for "Rhinestone Cowboy" in 1976. When accepting the award, he sounded "almost apologetic," seeming to confirm he was not from Nashville and expressed regret for winning despite being from New York. "Larry Weiss won the CMAs song of the year for Rhyne Stone cowboy in 1976. When he almost sounded apologetic when he accepted the award, it was seemingly like he needed to confirm that he was not from Nashville, and I'm so sorry that I'm from New York, and I won this award."

podcast.title: Diverse Songwriting Credits
podcast.body: Before writing "Rhinestone Cowboy," Larry Weiss wrote many songs in the 1960s for artists such as The Charelles, The Animals, and Jeff Beck. "He wrote many songs before he wrote Rhyne Stone cowboy in the 1960s. He wrote for the charelles. He wrote for the animals. Jeff Beck."

podcast.title: Queens, New York City Origin
podcast.body: Larry Weiss is from Queens, New York City. He wrote "Rhinestone Cowboy" after moving to LA, reflecting on his life and paying homage to cowboy movie heroes of his youth like Gene Autry. "Larry Weiss from? Well, he's from Queens, New York City."
